name: Comorian Langouste a la Vanille
description: Langouste à la vanille, lobster in a real vanilla-cream sauce, is one of Comoros's most iconic dishes, honoring the islands' status as a major vanilla producer - shrimp stands in here for lobster as a more widely available substitute.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic in a little butter or oil 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook 2-3 minutes until just turning pink.
Add the cream and vanilla, and simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.

name: Comorian Pilao
description: Pilao, spiced rice cooked with meat, reflects genuine Swahili coastal and Indian Ocean trade influence shared across Comoros and the wider East African coast.
steps_detailed: Deeply brown the onion, 10-12 minutes, until golden.
Add the chicken, cumin, and cinnamon, and brown 6-7 minutes.
Add the rice and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

name: Comorian Mataba
description: Mataba, cassava leaves cooked in real coconut milk, a genuine Comorian staple - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic in a little oil 30 seconds.
Add the spinach and coconut milk, and simmer 12-15 minutes until well combined.
